correctness.rationale: Exact beta integration gives the axial kernel coefficient normalization. The quartic Cayley transform and Routh first column are derived symbolically and checked by the standalone script. A direct imaginary-axis calculation excludes other crossings for all p>0. The only two boundary roots are simple, and the count on all open parameter intervals follows from Routh sign changes and continuity at its removable pivot degeneration p=1/2. Every disk product is attainable by two axial domain points. No global zero-free converse is claimed.

originality.rationale: The first-public 2017 radial-weight analysis establishes general kernel-zero phenomena, not this weight-specific census. The 2021 cylindrical-domain paper gives a general monomial/Lauricella kernel expansion, not the complete two-threshold four-cylinder axial root count. The closest published fourth-Jacobi-order classification treats a genuinely different moment sequence \((n+t)_5\) rather than \(\prod_{j=0}^4(n+1+jp)\). Its Routh analysis does not imply the present parameter thresholds. An earlier two-cylinder zero-free result covers p=1 but not variable axial power. Detailed scope, implications and accessibility risks follow.
residual_risks: The day of the earliest 2021 online appearance of Park is not verified; the motivating 2017 arXiv v1 date is exact and precedes it.
An unindexed general polynomial stability theorem could subsume the special quartic thresholds, even though none of the inspected exact statements does.
The theorem classifies the central axis only; it does not settle global zero-freeness in the high-parameter region.

value.rationale: The fourth-power cutoff weight is forced naturally by the cross-sectional geometry of a full intersection of four complex cylinders, not an arbitrary engineered radial polynomial. Its complete three-regime exact zero count and two simple sharp thresholds provide explicit Lu Qi-Keng obstructions across a continuous family, beyond a general kernel expansion, isolated examples or numerical tests.
